tasks.short: Keep employee benefit and pension records correct and sort out differences with brokers and providers.

today.trigger: A starter, leaver, contract change, provider invoice or employee benefit question arrives.
steps: Check employment dates, pay, hours and scheme eligibility in AFAS.
Prepare enrolments, changes and cancellations for the relevant provider.
Compare provider confirmations and invoices with AFAS and payroll deductions.
Resolve differences with Payroll, the employee, broker or provider.
Record the outcome and explain any action the employee must take.
systems: Provider and broker channels, to confirm
drudgery: Re-entering the same employment changes for several providers
Matching invoice lines to employee records
Chasing missing confirmations
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: inconsistent provider files and unresolved eligibility questions consume more time than routine enrolments.

lenses.faster: Rule-based checks and provider files remove most re-entry and line matching. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 30 minutes, comprising 12 minutes on exceptions, 10 with providers and eight reviewing results.
lenses.autonomous: An approved AFAS employment change or new provider file starts eligibility checks, reconciliation and preparation of routine changes. Validated changes can proceed under delegated authority; ambiguous eligibility, retrospective corrections and new scheme rules stop for approval.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give Payroll a monthly benefit-deduction reconciliation before payroll closes, including unresolved provider differences. Demand would grow if checking became cheaper because Payroll could request checks after significant employment changes too.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying dates, matching invoices or chasing routine acknowledgements. I would spend more time helping employees understand consequential pension and insurance choices.
lenses.options: Compare correcting a discrepancy this month, spreading an agreed recovery or asking the provider to reverse it. Showing employee cash effects and administrative costs can change which remedy we recommend.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts toward provider exceptions, scheme changes and employee support. With HR Director delegation, I could approve routine corrections within agreed limits; the remaining work becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the Payroll Specialist's routine reconciliation of benefit deductions; learn payroll cut-offs, correction rules and control totals.
Absorb the HR Administrator's provider enrolment preparation; learn each scheme's eligibility and required evidence.

tasks.human_edge: I must interpret disputed eligibility, recognise when a correction would harm an employee and challenge a provider whose records contradict the employment agreement.
tasks.pattern_why: Eligibility tables, effective dates, contribution formulas and reconciliation tolerances can be written down. AI can help build the checks, but routine execution does not need a model.

in_practice.trigger: An approved AFAS change or scheduled provider reconciliation.
steps: Read approved employment changes and provider files through authorised exports or confirmed interfaces.
Apply versioned scheme rules and compare contributions, deductions and effective dates.
Prepare or transmit routine changes where the provider interface and delegated authority permit.
Route missing evidence, unmatched records and retrospective corrections to the specialist.
Record acknowledgements and reconcile completed changes with Payroll.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves new rules and exceptions; routine transactions run only within tested eligibility rules and authorised transmission limits.
systems: Provider interfaces or file uploads, subject to validation
data_needed: Approved employment changes and payroll deductions
Scheme eligibility and contribution rules with effective dates
Provider member identifiers, statements and acknowledgements
Confirmed pension fund coverage for each employee group
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint reconciliation register, with transaction references attached to the relevant AFAS record.

evidence.claim: Rule-based reconciliation and eligibility checks are technically feasible; Noordhaven's provider interfaces and achievable savings remain untested.
Pensioenfonds Vervoer's overbruggingsplan describes an expected transition on 1 January 2027; Noordhaven's membership and the final implementation position need confirmation.

risks: Incorrect effective dates or scheme rules could interrupt cover or cause wrong deductions.
Provider interfaces may require manual uploads, reducing the estimated saving.
AVG/GDPR requires limited access and minimum necessary data; medical information must not enter this reconciliation.
Flex workers' benefits may be administered by their agency, requiring a different route.
research_questions: Which providers accept structured change files or APIs, and how do they acknowledge acceptance?
What share of current administration is routine matching versus disputed eligibility?
Which employee groups belong to which pension schemes, and what transition changes are confirmed?
Can a pilot reconcile a payroll month without missed changes or incorrect deductions?

tasks.short: Assess what a job actually involves and recommend its CAO classification and salary band.

today.trigger: A new vacancy, changed role or manager request requires a classification decision.
steps: Gather the job description, actual duties and manager explanation.
Identify the applicable CAO and job evaluation system.
Assess skills, responsibilities, effort and working conditions.
Compare the role with established reference jobs and salary bands.
Discuss the recommendation and record the approved classification.
drudgery: Turning inconsistent manager descriptions into comparable evidence
Finding previous evaluations of similar jobs
Rewriting factor explanations
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: incomplete descriptions and disagreements about actual responsibilities cause repeated interviews and revisions.

lenses.faster: One model call drafts a factor-by-factor assessment with evidence references and missing facts. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 39 minutes, comprising 20 minutes validating duties, 14 reviewing the grade and five recording the decision.
lenses.autonomous: An accepted evaluation request starts document assembly and a draft assessment. The specialist checks the work, decides the recommendation and obtains the required approval before any AFAS band changes.
lenses.ambitious: More frequent decision: review whether changing responsibilities warrant evaluation at a quarterly role-change review. Demand would grow as preparation becomes cheaper, but only material accountability changes should lead to regrading.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss searching old files or repeatedly rewriting the same factor rationale. I would spend more time understanding warehouse work and resolving difficult boundaries between jobs.
lenses.options: Compare two defensible grades and a redesigned role with narrower responsibilities. Seeing the evidence needed for each can change the job design itself, rather than simply increase the proposed salary.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts from assembling evaluation files to checking consistency across sites. With delegated authority, I could return unsupported requests and approve routine recommendations within the agreed framework; the role becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the HR Business Partner's initial job-analysis interviews; learn structured interviewing and how each site's responsibilities differ.
Absorb the Recruiter's preliminary vacancy-band check; learn vacancy requirements and offer approval limits.

tasks.human_edge: I must distinguish actual responsibility from an inflated description, understand physical and shift conditions and defend a grade to managers and employees.
tasks.pattern_why: A fixed workflow needs one conversion of messy job evidence into a checkable factor assessment. The model drafts; the specialist evaluates under the applicable CAO or agreed system.

in_practice.trigger: A manager submits an evaluation request with a description and evidence of changed duties.
steps: Collect the applicable CAO criteria, approved reference jobs and supplied job evidence.
Make one model call to draft factor assessments, evidence references and unanswered questions.
Check the actual duties with the manager and, where needed, employees doing the work.
Decide the recommendation and compare it with equivalent roles across sites.
Obtain approval and enter the agreed classification in AFAS.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist decides the assessment; the authorised manager approves the change. Changes to the evaluation system follow applicable CAO rules and OR consent requirements.
data_needed: Current job descriptions and evidence of actual duties
Applicable CAO classification criteria and salary tables
Approved reference evaluations
Skills, responsibilities, effort and working-condition evidence
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint evaluation register containing inputs, model version, draft, human reasoning and approval; final classification in AFAS.

evidence.claim: A self-reported university pilot assessed 50 job descriptions against HERA factors and reported accuracy exceeding 70%; it did not establish Dutch CAO accuracy or time savings.
AFAS Profit 8 offers job scheme and category fields as preparation for pay transparency; these fields do not perform job evaluation.
WOR Article 27 covers consent for remuneration or job evaluation systems, subject to the exceptions in Article 27(3).

risks: A persuasive but wrong factor assessment could create an unexplained pay difference.
US exempt/non-exempt labels do not map directly to Dutch employment rules; the workflow must use the applicable Dutch criteria.
CAO reference jobs or sector regrading may change, making stored criteria obsolete.
A model recommending grades or pay may fall within EU AI Act Annex III employment provisions; classification, commencement and oversight requirements need confirmation.
research_questions: Which evaluation system applies to transport, warehouse and office jobs, and which decisions are already settled by a CAO?
How closely do model drafts match independently assessed Noordhaven reference jobs, including shift and physical-work factors?
Does reviewing a draft actually take less time than assessing the job directly?
What AI Act obligations and OR arrangements apply to the proposed use at deployment?

tasks.short: Research benefits and workplace practices and recommend changes that suit our people, sites and CAOs.

today.trigger: A renewal, employee concern, absence trend or proposed policy change prompts a review.
steps: Define the problem with HR Business Partners and the relevant safety or occupational-health adviser.
Gather policies, benefit usage, costs and suitable external sources.
Compare practices with CAO requirements and the needs of each site and shift.
Develop options with costs, eligibility and implementation consequences.
Recommend a change and identify approvals or consultation needed.
drudgery: Reading overlapping policy and provider documents
Building comparable option tables
Checking whether apparently attractive benefits cover shift workers
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: checking source quality and translating general practices into workable site and shift arrangements.

lenses.faster: AI prepares source summaries and comparison tables while I verify the evidence and choose the recommendation. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 39 minutes, comprising 15 minutes checking sources, 14 judging options and 10 discussing feasibility.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled renewal or agreed research question starts a document pack and draft comparison. I direct the research and approve every recommendation; occupational-health and safety specialists assess matters within their remit.
lenses.ambitious: New group served: assess benefit access for night-shift workers at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. Demand would grow if comparisons became cheaper because site managers could request small access improvements between annual renewals.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss reading duplicate brochures or rebuilding comparison tables. I would spend more time listening to shift workers and testing whether a proposed benefit is useful to them.
lenses.options: Compare benefit redesign, a provider change and a targeted access pilot using the same budget. Differences in shift coverage and employee uptake can change the recommendation even when headline prices are similar.
lenses.altitude: My week includes more small policy experiments and fewer broad document searches. With HR Director delegation, I could select pilots within an approved budget; judgement becomes more expert through evaluation of actual outcomes.
reach: Absorb the HR Business Partner's initial benefit-usage review by site; learn employee consultation and how to interpret usage without exposing individuals.
Absorb the FP&A Analyst's first-pass benefit scenario costing; learn total employment costs and sensitivity analysis.

tasks.human_edge: I must recognise which practices fit Noordhaven's shifts, test employee acceptability and know when a safety or medical question belongs with a qualified specialist.
tasks.pattern_why: The specialist must choose the research direction, judge sources and reconcile cost, access and employee needs. AI supports those decisions with summaries and alternatives.

in_practice.trigger: The specialist opens a review for a named benefit or policy problem.
steps: Define the decision, employee groups, budget and evidence required.
Use AI to summarise selected current documents with traceable source references.
Build cost and access comparisons using verified figures.
Test the options with site representatives and relevant professional advisers.
Present the recommendation and required consultation or approval.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist checks all material claims and recommends the option; the HR Director and relevant advisers approve implementation, with OR involvement where required.
data_needed: Current benefit terms, eligibility and provider prices
Aggregated usage, absence and retention indicators
Shift patterns and employee feedback
Applicable CAO provisions and professional safety advice
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint policy-review file containing sources, assumptions, options, consultation findings and the approved decision.

evidence.claim: Models can summarise supplied policies and draft comparisons, but the digest provides no measured benefits-policy research case for this company context.
WOR Article 27 includes consent requirements for specified employment arrangements, including certain occupational-health and absence arrangements, subject to applicable exceptions.

risks: External examples may omit Dutch tax, CAO or shift-access constraints.
Small site or shift groups could make aggregated health information identifiable.
Benefit changes must not bypass professional safety assessment or Wet verbetering poortwachter responsibilities.
Cheaper research could produce more proposals than the team can implement or evaluate.
research_questions: Which benefits have low uptake because of eligibility, shift access or poor communication?
Can summaries be checked faster than the source documents can be read directly?
Which proposed changes require OR consent, professional advice or tax review?
Can a small pilot measure improved access or uptake without collecting unnecessary health data?

tasks.short: Explain Dutch employment rules, CAOs, pay and benefits to managers and employees.

today.trigger: A manager or employee asks about pay, benefits, classification or an employment procedure.
steps: Clarify the question and the person's employment and CAO context.
Find the current policy, agreement or statutory guidance.
Check relevant AFAS facts where individual circumstances matter.
Explain the answer and practical next steps.
Refer disputed or specialist matters and record the advice.
drudgery: Finding the same clauses repeatedly
Rewriting familiar explanations
Clarifying questions that omit contract or CAO details
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: identifying the applicable agreement and explaining exceptions takes longer than retrieving standard policy text.

lenses.faster: AI finds relevant supplied clauses and drafts a plain answer with references. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 36 minutes, comprising 12 minutes clarifying context, 16 on individual advice and eight checking the reply.
lenses.autonomous: A question opens a draft workspace with likely sources and missing facts. I lead the conversation and approve the answer; individual legal interpretations and pay consequences do not become automatic replies.
lenses.ambitious: New group served: offer night-shift employees asynchronous pay and benefits advice they can access outside office hours. Demand would grow as access gets easier, so the service needs a clear response queue and escalation route.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss hunting clauses or typing the same explanation again. I would spend more time helping people understand their choices and resolving confusing exceptions.
lenses.options: Draft a standard-policy answer, an exception request and a referral where all three are plausible. Comparing their consequences helps me decide which route fits the employee's circumstances.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts toward difficult advice and improving the explanations that cause repeated questions. With delegated authority, I could close standard interpretation cases within approved guidance; the remaining advice becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the HR Administrator's first-line benefits and pay-policy questions; learn case handling, identity checks and referral boundaries.
Absorb the HR Business Partner's preparation of standard compensation advice; learn manager context and escalation thresholds.

tasks.human_edge: I must notice when the stated question hides a dispute or personal hardship, weigh competing interpretations and take responsibility for advice that affects someone's income.
tasks.pattern_why: Advice depends on context, trust and interpretation. A source-backed draft helps, but the specialist remains the lead throughout the exchange.

in_practice.trigger: A pay or benefits question reaches the authorised HR channel.
steps: Clarify the applicable employee group, CAO and question with the specialist.
Retrieve approved, effective policy documents and only necessary employee facts.
Draft an answer with clause references, assumptions and any missing information.
Have the specialist check the interpretation, personalise the answer and send it.
Record the advice and assign any referral or follow-up.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist reviews each individual answer before it is sent and refers legal disputes, pension choices and occupational-health matters to the appropriate expert.
data_needed: Current CAOs, policies and benefit documents with effective dates
Approved interpretation notes and escalation routes
Minimum necessary employment facts
Question history and unresolved follow-up
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint advice register with source versions and the final response; relevant employment actions recorded in AFAS.

evidence.claim: Source-backed drafting can reduce repeated policy lookup and writing; the savings estimate is unmeasured at Noordhaven.
AI Act Article 50 contains disclosure requirements relevant if this service later becomes a directly interacting benefits chatbot; applicability and commencement must be checked.
The digest's Dutch pay-transparency source describes employee pay-information rights; implementation timing and the final Dutch requirements require verification.

risks: A correct clause from the wrong CAO or effective date could produce wrong advice.
Salary and benefit details could leak through excessive model access or shared Teams channels.
Flex workers may need advice from their agency rather than a Noordhaven employment-policy answer.
An absence-related question could expose medical information or require referral under Wet verbetering poortwachter procedures.
research_questions: What share of questions is answered by approved guidance without a new interpretation?
Can the draft reliably identify the correct CAO, effective date and missing facts?
How much demand would night-shift access add, and can the specialist handle the exceptions?
Do access controls prevent answers from exposing another employee's personal information?

tasks.short: Design and run pay increases and incentives within our CAOs, budget and agreed approval rules.

today.trigger: An annual pay review, CAO increase or proposed incentive scheme needs design or administration.
steps: Confirm eligibility, CAO obligations, budget and programme objectives.
Gather pay, contracted hours, approved assessments and relevant performance measures.
Calculate proposed awards and identify inconsistent outcomes.
Compare programme designs with managers, Finance and HR leadership.
Secure approval, instruct Payroll and prepare employee communications.
drudgery: Combining pay and eligibility spreadsheets
Recalculating totals after each budget change
Preparing repeated manager and employee explanations
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: manager revisions, eligibility exceptions and disagreement about fair incentives dominate the cycle.

lenses.faster: Controlled calculations remove spreadsheet rebuilding, while AI helps compare designs and draft explanations. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 42 minutes, comprising 15 minutes validating awards, 17 judging the design and 10 on approval and communication.
lenses.autonomous: An approved review calendar or CAO change starts eligibility and costing drafts. I lead programme design, managers explain their proposals and authorised leaders approve awards before Payroll receives instructions.
lenses.ambitious: More frequent decision: review whether incentive rules are distorting safety or retention at a quarterly programme review. Demand would grow if analysis became cheaper, particularly when site managers can test changes before the next cycle.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding award sheets after every budget change. I would spend more time designing incentives that support safe operations and retain productive hires beyond 90 days.
lenses.options: Compare flat increases, band-position adjustments and team incentives under the same budget. Showing who gains, who is excluded and which behaviours are rewarded can change the programme selected.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts toward incentive design and challenges to inconsistent awards. With HR Director and Finance delegation, I could reject out-of-policy submissions and recommend reallocations; the role becomes more expert.
reach: Absorb the FP&A Analyst's initial compensation-budget scenarios; learn forecasting assumptions and employer on-costs.
Absorb the HR Business Partner's preparation of manager pay-review packs; learn calibration and how to challenge weak evidence.

tasks.human_edge: I must judge whether an incentive rewards useful work, encourages unsafe behaviour or disguises favouritism, and help managers defend individual outcomes.
tasks.pattern_why: Programme design and award judgements stay with people. Deterministic calculations and AI drafts support a specialist-led review rather than determine individual pay.

in_practice.trigger: An authorised pay-review cycle or incentive-design request.
steps: Freeze the approved eligibility rules, pay snapshot, budget and CAO requirements.
Calculate scenarios in controlled formulas and reconcile totals with Finance.
Use AI to draft comparisons and explanations from verified scenario outputs.
Review fairness, behaviour incentives and manager exceptions with the specialist leading.
Obtain programme and award approvals before sending controlled instructions to Payroll.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist recommends the design; authorised leaders approve individual awards and budgets. Relevant system changes follow CAO and OR requirements.
data_needed: Approved pay and contracted-hours snapshot
CAO increases, eligibility rules and salary bands
Approved performance evidence and programme objectives
Budget, employer on-costs and prior awards
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint compensation-cycle register with scenario versions, reasons, exceptions and approvals; approved payroll mutations in AFAS.

evidence.claim: Controlled formulas can cost awards and validate eligibility, but the digest contains no documented Dutch AI merit-cycle result.
The Payscale survey reports differing approaches to paying for AI skills; it does not establish an appropriate premium for Noordhaven.
WOR consent requirements can apply to remuneration systems, with exceptions where a CAO already settles the matter.

risks: Historic performance assessments can carry bias into apparently precise award proposals.
Warehouse productivity incentives could encourage unsafe work or penalise legitimate absence.
Model-generated individual pay recommendations may trigger EU AI Act employment requirements; solely automated significant decisions raise GDPR Article 22 concerns.
A draft award or communication could be mistaken for an approved payroll instruction.
research_questions: Which awards are fixed by CAO rules, and where does Noordhaven have actual discretion?
Do approved performance measures reflect safe work and retention rather than only throughput?
Can the scenario process reduce preparation time without increasing correction work?
Which AI Act, GDPR and OR requirements apply to each proposed model use?

tasks.short: Help resolve employee complaints about job grades and salary with clear evidence and a fair hearing.

today.trigger: An employee, manager, HR Business Partner or works council representative raises a classification or salary complaint.
steps: Hear the complaint and clarify the outcome the employee seeks.
Gather the contract, pay history, evaluation and applicable CAO evidence.
Check comparable roles and the reasons for any difference.
Discuss possible remedies with the relevant decision-makers.
Explain the recommendation, record the outcome and identify any appeal route.
drudgery: Reconstructing the history from scattered records
Preparing chronology and comparison tables
Drafting repeated procedural explanations
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: contested facts, trust and agreement on a remedy consume most of the time.

lenses.faster: AI drafts a chronology and evidence table, reducing file assembly. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 48 minutes, comprising 20 minutes hearing the case, 18 assessing it and 10 agreeing and explaining the next step.
lenses.autonomous: The specialist opens a case and requests an evidence draft after clarifying the complaint. I control the investigation and recommendation; no model decides the complaint or sends a settlement.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give HR Business Partners an early review of whether the evidence supports a disputed grade before positions harden. Demand would grow if preparation became cheaper, allowing earlier intervention in emerging disputes.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss reconstructing email histories or formatting comparison tables. I would spend more time hearing employees properly and helping both sides reach a defensible resolution.
lenses.options: Compare a corrected grade, back pay, revised duties and a supported decision to retain the grade. Their evidence requirements and consequences can change the remedy recommended.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts toward early dispute advice and recurring fairness problems. With delegated authority, I could require missing evidence and recommend standard remedies within limits; the work becomes more expert and remains human-led.
reach: Absorb the HR Business Partner's compensation-case chronology and first evidence review; learn complaint procedures, interviewing and conflict handling.
Absorb the Payroll Specialist's initial estimate of a proposed back-pay correction; learn effective dates, payroll corrections and tax boundaries.

tasks.human_edge: I must hear contested accounts, recognise unequal bargaining power, challenge weak management explanations and recommend a remedy people can trust.
tasks.pattern_why: The result depends on disputed facts, procedural fairness and accountable judgement. AI can assemble and explain evidence but cannot responsibly produce nearly all of the resolution advice.

in_practice.trigger: The specialist registers a complaint and defines the evidence needed.
steps: Hear the employee and record the complaint without model-generated credibility judgements.
Collect authorised records and draft a referenced chronology and comparison table.
Check omissions, disputed facts and comparator suitability with the specialist.
Develop possible remedies and obtain the authorised decision.
Explain the outcome personally and record follow-up or appeal steps.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist conducts the substantive assessment and recommends the remedy; the authorised decision-maker approves it before communication or payroll action.
data_needed: Employee complaint and requested outcome
Contract, pay history and prior evaluation
Applicable CAO and complaint procedure
Relevant comparator evidence with restricted personal details
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint complaint file with evidence references, contested facts, human reasoning, approvals and final response.

evidence.claim: Models can draft chronologies from supplied documents, but the digest provides no case showing automated resolution of Dutch classification or salary complaints.
The digest's Dutch pay-transparency source describes rights to pay information and mechanisms for addressing unexplained differences; the final Dutch position needs verification.
AI Act Annex III identifies employment uses that may cover systems influencing pay-related decisions; legal classification depends on the actual use.

risks: A confident summary could omit evidence that supports the employee.
Comparator data could expose another employee's salary or personal circumstances.
Using AI to judge credibility or recommend a settlement could undermine procedural fairness.
Extra model review may consume the modest expected saving in complex cases.
research_questions: How much complaint time is document assembly versus interviews, judgement and negotiation?
Can drafts preserve contradictory evidence and flag missing records without inventing a conclusion?
Which comparator details may be disclosed under the procedure and AVG/GDPR?
Do employees and their representatives accept this limited evidence-preparation use?

tasks.short: Write consistent job descriptions and maintain classifications and salary scales across our three sites.

today.trigger: A vacancy, organisational change, approved evaluation or CAO salary-table update requires revised documentation.
steps: Collect actual duties, manager input and existing role documents.
Draft the description using the agreed job-family structure.
Check classification criteria and approved salary tables.
Resolve inconsistent titles, responsibilities or bands across sites.
Approve and publish the documents and update AFAS and vacancy information.
drudgery: Reformatting manager drafts
Maintaining duplicate descriptions and salary tables
Checking whether vacancies use the latest approved band
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: inconsistent site descriptions and uncertainty about the authoritative version create repeated revisions.

lenses.faster: One model call drafts a standard description and highlights missing factor evidence; fixed lookups populate approved scale information. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 33 minutes, comprising 15 minutes validating duties, 10 checking classification and eight approving and publishing.
lenses.autonomous: An accepted document-change request starts a draft and comparison with the previous version. I approve the content and band references before publication; substantive grade changes follow the separate evaluation process.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give Recruiters an approved role and band pack before opening a vacancy. Demand would grow as preparation gets cheaper because hiring managers could request clearer packs for hard-to-fill warehouse and transport roles.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss reformatting descriptions or correcting obsolete salary-table copies. I would spend more time clarifying career steps between jobs and making responsibilities understandable.
lenses.options: Compare a single cross-site role, site-specific variants and a role split with different accountabilities. Those drafts can change the job structure and recruitment proposition before a grade is requested.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts toward job-family consistency, career paths and change control. With delegated authority, I could approve editorial updates and block vacancies using obsolete bands; decisions about material job changes become more expert.
reach: Absorb the Recruiter's factual vacancy-description preparation; learn candidate-facing clarity and the Recruitee publishing process.
Absorb the HR Administrator's maintenance of approved job records; learn AFAS job-scheme fields and effective-date controls.

tasks.human_edge: I must confirm that descriptions reflect real work, preserve meaningful differences between sites and prevent neat wording from concealing changed accountability.
tasks.pattern_why: The main messy-input step is turning manager evidence into a consistent description. One checkable draft is sufficient; salary scales remain exact lookups from approved sources.

in_practice.trigger: An authorised role-document request or approved salary-table change.
steps: Collect manager evidence, the current description, approved templates and applicable scale data.
Make one model call to draft the description, highlight differences and list missing facts.
Validate duties and working conditions with the manager and relevant employees.
Attach the approved classification and salary scale through controlled lookups.
Approve the version, publish it in SharePoint and update AFAS and Recruitee references.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves every published description and salary reference; the manager confirms actual duties, and changed classifications require the evaluation approval process.
data_needed: Approved templates and job-family definitions
Evidence of actual duties and working conditions
Approved evaluations and CAO salary tables
Effective dates, owners and previous document versions
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint job-architecture register with draft changes, sources and approvals; final job fields in AFAS and approved vacancy references in Recruitee.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 provides job scheme and category fields that can support consistent records; the digest does not show automated description generation.
The Payscale survey reports that employers are revising job descriptions while salary structures lag; it demonstrates stated demand, not measured workflow savings.
The cited practice discussion cautions against regrading every AI-related change where core accountabilities have not materially changed.

risks: Standardisation could erase real differences in effort, responsibility or working conditions.
A description could drift beyond the approved evaluation and imply an unsupported band.
Outdated salary tables could enter vacancy packs or employee documents.
Changing the job or pay system may require CAO alignment and OR consent rather than simple document approval.
research_questions: How many descriptions are duplicates, obsolete or inconsistent across sites?
Can managers validate drafts with fewer revisions than the current process?
Which AFAS job-scheme fields are available in Noordhaven's installed version?
Can one authoritative salary-table source keep AFAS, SharePoint and Recruitee references consistent?

tasks.short: Cost pay and CAO proposals and explain their effects on employees, sites and the company budget.

today.trigger: HR leadership, Finance or negotiators request the cost of a pay or CAO proposal.
steps: Clarify the proposal, comparison baseline and negotiation assumptions.
Gather payroll, hours, allowances, employer contributions and relevant agency costs.
Reconcile the population and totals with Payroll and Finance.
Calculate scenarios by employee group, site and effective date.
Explain the results, sensitivities and unresolved assumptions.
drudgery: Rebuilding employee populations and cost formulas
Recalculating similar proposals
Reconciling different payroll and finance definitions
today.time_sinks: Assumed current workflow: reconciling inputs and repeating calculations after small proposal changes account for much of the preparation.

lenses.faster: A versioned calculation model removes repeated extraction, formula rebuilding and scenario recalculation. Planning estimate: each current hour becomes 27 minutes, comprising eight minutes reconciling totals, 11 challenging assumptions and eight briefing decision-makers.
lenses.autonomous: An approved proposal entered into a standard scenario form starts calculations and a draft results pack. The specialist checks assumptions and reconciliation exceptions before the figures are used in negotiations.
lenses.ambitious: More frequent decision: cost counterproposals during a bargaining session rather than waiting for a later spreadsheet revision. Demand would grow if recalculation became cheaper because negotiators could compare more feasible trade-offs.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding formulas or discovering incompatible headcount totals late in the process. I would spend more time explaining which proposal is affordable and which employee groups are affected.
lenses.options: Compare percentage rises, fixed-euro increases, shift allowances and phased effective dates within the same envelope. Distribution and recurring cost differences can change the bargaining position selected.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts from spreadsheet production to testing affordability and negotiation assumptions. With Finance delegation, I could certify reconciled costing packs within approved assumptions; analytical expertise increases while negotiation authority stays explicitly assigned.
reach: Absorb the FP&A Analyst's detailed workforce-cost scenario calculation; learn forecast conventions, employer on-costs and agency pricing.
Absorb the Controller's preparation of payroll-to-ledger cost reconciliations; learn ledger mappings and timing differences.

tasks.human_edge: I must challenge unrealistic staffing and overtime assumptions, distinguish permanent costs from temporary ones and explain consequences negotiators may otherwise overlook.
tasks.pattern_why: The proposal parameters, effective dates and cost formulas are explicit and testable. A calculation engine can run without a model; interpretation and negotiation remain with people.

in_practice.trigger: An authorised user submits a complete proposal using approved scenario parameters.
steps: Load a dated AFAS payroll extract and approved agency-cost inputs.
Reconcile the population and baseline costs with Payroll and Finance control totals.
Apply versioned CAO, allowance, contribution and effective-date formulas.
Generate scenario comparisons, sensitivities and exception flags.
Have the specialist approve the costing pack before negotiation or budget use.
in_practice.human_gate: New formulas and assumptions require specialist and Finance approval. Routine calculations run unattended, but every externally used negotiation pack receives human approval.
data_needed: Dated payroll population, contracted hours and actual paid components
CAO tables, allowances, pension contributions and employer on-costs
Agency rates, hours and contractual price-adjustment rules
Approved proposal parameters, baseline and Finance control totals
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint costing register with extract dates, formula versions, scenario parameters, reconciliation results and approval.

evidence.claim: Explicit pay and employer-cost formulas can be automated and reconciled; the digest provides no measured Noordhaven implementation result.
The cited CNV update describes sector job-regrading work; it supplies context for changing assumptions rather than a final replacement classification or costing table.

risks: Missing overtime, allowances or employer contributions could materially understate costs.
Agency prices may react differently from employee salaries and must follow agency contracts.
The nightly AFAS extract cannot support a genuinely current bargaining baseline without a fresh controlled extract.
Faster scenarios could create false precision when staffing volumes and implementation dates remain uncertain.
research_questions: Can the baseline reconcile to payroll and the general ledger across all three sites?
Which cost components and agency adjustments are absent from the current model?
Can approved counterproposals be calculated quickly enough for live bargaining without changing formulas?
How much current effort is repeated calculation versus negotiation and assumption-setting?

role.altitude: The role becomes the specialist responsible for consistent job architecture and defensible pay differences across Noordhaven's three sites. The week contains more difficult evaluations, employee advice, provider exceptions and compensation design; delegated rights could cover routine corrections, document approval and certified costing, while programme and individual pay decisions retain their authorised approvers.
reach: Payroll Specialist: benefit-deduction reconciliation and initial back-pay costing, after learning payroll controls and correction rules.
HR Administrator: provider-change preparation and approved job-record maintenance, after learning scheme eligibility and AFAS effective-date controls.
Recruiter: approved vacancy role and band packs, after learning Recruitee publication and offer approval requirements.
HR Business Partner: initial job-analysis interviews and compensation-case evidence preparation, after learning consultation and complaint procedures.
FP&A Analyst and Controller: workforce-cost scenarios and initial payroll-to-ledger reconciliation, after learning finance definitions and control totals.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks cover 870.6 hours annually. The planning estimates release about 340 hours, roughly 21% of the implied 1,600-hour role year, worth about EUR 25,500 of capacity at EUR 75/hour; this is neither a measured result nor a cash saving. Provider interfaces, manager interviews, complaints, negotiations, CAO boundaries and approvals limit further savings, and new services would use part of the released capacity.

role.ambitious_version: Provide Recruiters with approved role and band packs, shift workers with accessible benefits advice, Payroll with reconciled benefit deductions and leadership with rapid, defensible pay scenarios. Connect those services to offer acceptance and 90-day retention, while monitoring unexplained pay differences and timely information responses under confirmed Dutch requirements. Expand decision support and employee access without making individual grades, awards or complaint outcomes solely automated.
